title: Tickeron AI flagged SLS on a Phase 3 AML vaccine win — then it jumped156%. Would your model have caught it?
author: tickeron_community
selftext:
Tickeron AI flagged \[SLS\]([https://tickeron.com/ticker/SLS/](https://tickeron.com/ticker/SLS/)) as one of  
Tuesday's biggest movers after galinpepimut-S, SELLAS's cancer  
vaccine, hit the primary overall survival endpoint of the Phase 3  
REGAL trial in AML.  
  
The move was yesterday (Tuesday, Nov 17), not today: SLS closed at  
$19.15, up 156% from Monday's $7.47 close. It's holding most of that  
gain today (Wednesday, Nov 18) around $18.40.  
  
The numbers: median overall survival came in at 24.0 months vs 14.7 on  
standard treatment — a 41% lower risk of death — with no new safety  
signals. For a company with no approved product, that Phase 3 win is  
the whole story.  
  
What's next: an FDA meeting on an accelerated pathway, a BLA planned  
for 1H 2027, and more data at ASH Dec 12–15. After hours Tuesday they  
also announced a $150M offering, which is why today's tape is a bit  
softer.  
  
Full write-up: [https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-sellas-life-sciences-group-sls-stock-up-157-03-today-39901/](https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-sellas-life-sciences-group-sls-stock-up-157-03-today-39901/)  
  
Would your model have caught this before the close — on the Phase 3  
readout itself, or only after the tape started running? And how would  
you treat the $150M offering in a post-gap setup?
